The relay can no longer read what it carries.

## 🔒 Changed

- **Everything the app sends through the relay is now encrypted end to end.** A second key comes out of the same twelve words, under its own domain, and every request and every answer is sealed with AES-256-GCM before it leaves the phone. The relay sees which instance a message is for, because it has to route it, and nothing else: not the path, not the body, and not the access token the app attaches.
- **That token was the reason this was worth doing.** A relay operator reading a task list learns what somebody downloaded; a relay operator reading a token can keep using it afterwards. It travelled in the clear until now. It does not any more.
- **The two keys are deliberately separate.** The relay is handed the group key in every hello frame, so a frame key derived from that value would be one it already holds. Deriving it from the phrase's secret under a different domain means the relay can hold one and never compute the other.
- **A frame cannot be redirected.** The fields the relay routes on are bound into the encryption, so a sealed call addressed to one instance will not open at another.

## 📋 Notes

- **This version cannot talk to instances older than it, and they cannot talk to it.** The frame format changed, so the whole group has to be on the new build: update your instances alongside the app. An instance running the old server will simply ignore what this app sends.
- **`versionCode` is 4.** It goes up on every build handed to anybody - it is what Android decides upgrade order by, and two builds sharing one are indistinguishable to a phone.
- **No reinstall needed.** Same signing key as before, so this installs over the existing app and keeps its connections.
- **The encryption is not a reason to point the app at somebody else's relay.** It closes the operator's window into your traffic, but a relay you do not run is still a machine deciding whether your instances meet at all. Use a named, revocable API token rather than an account password either way.
- **One case stays weaker, and it is not the phrase.** A connection configured with a hand-entered relay key instead of a phrase has no secret to derive from, so its frame key comes from the relay key itself - which seals the traffic against anything between the app and the relay, but not against the relay's operator. The connect screen never uses that path.
